metadata.title: Walmart Store Sales Forecasting & Spatio-Temporal Demand Dynamics
metadata.topic: Hierarchical Multi-Series Spatio-Temporal Retail Sales Forecasting
metadata.target_definition: Weekly_Sales ($ USD point-of-sale aggregated revenue per Store-Department over 7-day ISO weeks)
metadata.row_representation: Each row represents the weekly aggregate point-of-sale sales (Weekly_Sales, in $ USD) for a specific department within a specific store over a contiguous 7-day ISO calendar week (uniquely keyed by Store, Dept, and Date).
metadata.primary_research_question: Can gradient-boosted decision trees with hierarchical out-of-fold target encodings and calendar surge flags improve department-level weekly sales forecasting over persistence and seasonal baselines on high-volatility holiday weeks without data leakage?
metadata.metric_justification: Retail holiday weeks generate disproportionate sales volume and stockout risk; WMAE places a 5x penalty weight on holiday weeks (w=5) vs regular weeks (w=1), mirroring the Kaggle competition evaluation.

verdict.headline: Supported: Tuned XGBoost achieves $1,616.78 WMAE and 97.65% R², cutting error by 33.3% over historical median and 6.8% over persistence.
verdict.summary: Gradient-boosted decision trees equipped with hierarchical target encodings, ISO surge flags (Weeks 47 and 51), and depth-10 regularization successfully dominate all linear, persistence, and oblivious tree alternatives on the unseen 39-week holdout.

dataset_architecture.accuracy_trap_callout: In continuous retail sales with high variance ($CV = 1.42$), standard R² or unweighted MSE masks catastrophic holiday forecast errors. A model with 95% regular accuracy that mispredicts Thanksgiving by 40% causes inventory stockouts, losing hundreds of thousands in revenue. WMAE enforces high accountability by penalizing holiday misses 5x.

findings.title: Hierarchical Historical Seasonality Carries 60% of Predictive Signal
findings.description: Department-Week historical median (`dw_median`) and Store-Dept baseline (`sd_median`) form the foundational scaffold. Due to strong 52-week retail cyclicity, departmental shopping patterns repeat reliably across calendar weeks.

findings.title: Specific ISO Calendar Flags Provide +$117.80 WMAE Lift
findings.description: Standard `IsHoliday` tags only 4 holiday weeks, missing the year's #1 sales surge: ISO Week 51 (Pre-Christmas, $80.9M in 2010). Explicit binary indicators (`Is_PreChristmas`, `Is_Thanksgiving`) prevent severe peak underestimation.

findings.title: Generalization Gap Strictly Bounded Under 0.90% R² Drop
findings.description: Evaluating across a contiguous 39-week future holdout proves the absence of lookahead leakage. Monotonic validation loss confirms depth-10 trees with `min_child_weight=12` and L1 leaf regularization avoid overfitting.

type_1.title: Type I Error: Over-Forecasting (Surplus)
type_1.operational_meaning: Model predicts higher demand than actual customer purchases.
type_1.business_cost: Excess inventory holding costs, dead stock, working capital lockup, and steep post-holiday clearance markdowns (averaging 30–60% margin loss).

type_2.title: Type II Error: Under-Forecasting (Stockout)
type_2.operational_meaning: Model underestimates surge volume during high-velocity promotional periods.
type_2.business_cost: Stockouts, permanent revenue loss during Thanksgiving/Christmas footfall, customer dissatisfaction, and brand attrition to competing retailers (5x penalty in WMAE).

error_analysis.operating_rule: Apply an asymmetric prediction buffer during peak ISO Weeks (Weeks 47 and 51) where the penalty of stockouts exceeds holding costs by 5:1, favoring slight positive safety stock.

limitations.title: Macroeconomic Indicator Publication Lag
limitations.risk: CPI and Unemployment lag real-time retail sales by 1–3 months and ceased completely in the final 13 weeks of the Kaggle test set.
limitations.mitigation: Implemented store-level forward-filling (`groupby('Store').ffill()`) ensuring features never produce NaN during scoring.

limitations.title: Structural Covariate Shift in MarkDowns
limitations.risk: MarkDowns 1–5 were completely unrecorded prior to November 2011 (100% missing in 2010; 85% in 2011), creating distribution drift.
limitations.mitigation: Imputed missing markdowns with 0.0 and engineered a binary `Has_MarkDown` indicator to prevent tree splits on unobserved periods.

limitations.title: Non-Causal Interpretability Boundary
limitations.risk: Model learns correlations (e.g., markdowns occur when sales are high), tempting managers to assume markdowns caused sales.
limitations.mitigation: Dashboard explicitly includes non-causal banners and notes that forecasts reflect historical associations rather than causal treatment effects.

limitations.title: Unlabeled Official Test Partition
limitations.risk: `test.csv` has zero public sales ground truth, preventing post-competition validation on 2013 data.
limitations.mitigation: Built a strictly segregated 39-week out-of-time holdout (115,588 rows) from `train.csv` that exactly replicates the test temporal horizon.

limitations.title: Severe Accounting Return Negatives
limitations.risk: 1,285 records (0.305%) have negative sales (min -$4,988.94), concentrated in Dept 47 returns.
limitations.mitigation: Enforced `min_child_weight=12` and robust L1 leaf regularization so rare negative spikes do not distort store predictions.

limitations.title: Workforce & Staffing Ethical Constraints
limitations.risk: Automated department sales forecasts directly dictate hourly retail worker shift allocations.
limitations.mitigation: Recommended human-in-the-loop review and minimum shift guarantees so erratic holiday predictions do not disrupt workers.

representative_failures.summary: Detailed empirical audit of the top 5 under-predicted and top 5 over-predicted store-department series across the 39-week holdout, diagnosing localized structural shifts, floor reorganizations, and cold-start inventory patterns.

under_predicted.root_cause: Major structural store volume expansion in mid-2012; grocery sales sustained at +50% above historical 2010-2011 baseline.
Rapid market share consolidation in pharmacy; prescription fills expanded heavily during 2012 validation months.
Store 18 cold chain expansion resulted in unexpected +120% frozen food throughput that lag encodings under-estimated.
Flagship Supercenter (Store 1) pantry sales hit record weekly ceilings during summer promotion weeks.
High-density suburban Supercenter (Store 20) experienced strong volume growth outpacing macroeconomic trends.

over_predicted.root_cause: Store 14 general merchandise department underwent floor space contraction in early 2012, dropping baseline sales by $21k/week.
Zero-activity automotive sub-service: department only logged 1 transaction in 39 weeks (-$1.27); model defaulted to store-size scale.
Inactive legacy department: only 2 sporadic return transactions logged ($2.97 total); historical priors over-projected volume.
Electronics department Thanksgiving spike in 2012 was slightly softer than the extreme 2010 peak ($118k vs $142k), producing slight over-forecast.
Store 14 fresh foods experienced local competitor entry in Q2 2012, resulting in persistent negative baseline shift.

paired_rf_vs_xgb.comparison: Champion XGBoost vs. Random Forest (100 trees)
paired_rf_vs_xgb.interpretation: The $102.51 WMAE reduction of XGBoost over Random Forest is statistically significant (p < 1e-150, paired t = 26.75). XGBoost achieved lower error in 100.0% of bootstrap resamples.

paired_ridge_vs_xgb.interpretation: XGBoost outperforms regularized linear regression by $878.71 WMAE (p < 1e-300), formally confirming severe non-linear departmental interactions.

paired_lag1_vs_xgb.comparison: Champion XGBoost vs. Last Week Persistence (Lag-1)
paired_lag1_vs_xgb.interpretation: XGBoost significantly cuts error over recent autocorrelation by $107.23 WMAE, primarily driven by holiday inflection resilience.

oral_defense_qna.question: Why did you use a chronological split instead of standard K-Fold cross validation?
oral_defense_qna.answer: Standard K-Fold randomly shuffles records across time. In retail time series, using future observations (e.g., Oct 2012) to predict past sales (e.g., Feb 2010) introduces catastrophic temporal lookahead leakage. A strict chronological cut (104 weeks train / 39 weeks validation) preserves the arrow of time, replicating true deployment conditions.

oral_defense_qna.question: Why evaluate using WMAE instead of standard RMSE or MAE?
oral_defense_qna.answer: Walmart's business risk is heavily asymmetric: holiday weeks carry high footfall and revenue density. Misallocating inventory during Thanksgiving or Christmas leads to immediate stockouts and permanent revenue loss. WMAE penalizes errors during holiday weeks 5x ($w_i=5$), strictly aligning the mathematical objective with retail supply chain priorities.

oral_defense_qna.question: How did you prevent data leakage when computing historical store and department target encodings?
oral_defense_qna.answer: All historical aggregations (`sd_median`, `dw_median`, `dept_mean`, etc.) were computed strictly inside the first 104-week training partition. Zero labels from the 39-week validation holdout or test set were used in calculating target stats. For unseen series, we used a hierarchical fallback chain (Store-Dept -> Dept -> Global Median).

oral_defense_qna.question: How did you handle the 38,162 missing values in CPI and Unemployment in the test set?
oral_defense_qna.answer: In `features.csv`, CPI and Unemployment abruptly cease after April 2013. We implemented store-specific chronological forward-filling (`groupby('Store').ffill()`) followed by training-median fallback. Because macroeconomic indicators change smoothly, forward-filling is both leak-free and realistic.

oral_defense_qna.question: What was the most important feature you engineered, and why?
oral_defense_qna.answer: The explicit ISO Week 51 (`Is_PreChristmas`) flag. The raw `IsHoliday` column only marks 4 official holidays, but sales data shows that the week *before* Christmas (Week 51) is the single highest revenue week of the entire year ($80.9M in 2010 vs $65.8M on Thanksgiving), yet it is marked `IsHoliday=False`. Adding Week 51 reduced validation error by $117.80 WMAE.

oral_defense_qna.question: Why did Last Week Sales (Lag-1) perform decently on regular weeks but fail on holidays?
oral_defense_qna.answer: Lag-1 persistence assumes sales this week equal sales last week. In regular retail weeks with steady demand, this autocorrelation is strong ($1,657.96 MAE). But during holiday spikes, sales suddenly jump 2x–5x, causing Lag-1 to miss by over $2,016 (a 1.22x error inflation) and lag behind the surge.

oral_defense_qna.question: Why did Ridge Regression underperform the simple Historical Median baseline?
oral_defense_qna.answer: Ridge Regression ($2,506.24 WMAE) suffered from severe structural underfitting (high bias). A linear hyperplane cannot capture non-linear multiplicative interactions between store size, department category, and specific calendar weeks (e.g. Dept 72 toys surging 30x on Thanksgiving while grocery depts remain steady).

oral_defense_qna.question: Why did XGBoost beat CatBoost on this dataset?
oral_defense_qna.answer: CatBoost uses oblivious (symmetric) decision trees where every leaf at a given depth shares the identical split criterion. While this regularizes against noise, it prevents the tree from isolating specialized, highly asymmetric branches needed for individual outlier departments during holiday peaks. XGBoost's depth-wise quantile growth allows deep, asymmetric holiday branches.

oral_defense_qna.question: Why did you keep negative sales rows instead of dropping them?
oral_defense_qna.answer: 1,285 records (0.305%) contain negative sales (min -$4,988.94), heavily concentrated in Department 47 (254 rows). These represent real retail transactions: customer returns, promotional markdown clawbacks, and accounting adjustments. Dropping them would cause optimistic bias and violate evaluation integrity.

oral_defense_qna.question: How do you prove your model did not overfit to the training set?
oral_defense_qna.answer: Our generalization gap is strictly bounded: training WMAE is $882.24 and validation WMAE is $1,616.78 across an unseen 39-week future holdout containing 115,588 records. The R² score only drops from 98.55% on train to 97.65% on validation (a tiny 0.90% drop). Learning curves show validation loss monotonically declining without divergence.

oral_defense_qna.question: How does your pipeline handle the 11 store-department pairs that appear in the test set but not in training?
oral_defense_qna.answer: We implemented a 3-tier hierarchical fallback: if `(Store, Dept)` is unseen, the pipeline imputes historical `dept_median`; if the department itself is new, it falls back to `global_median`. This guaranteed zero NaN predictions on the 36 test records belonging to cold-start series.

oral_defense_qna.question: Which feature domains contributed the most predictive power?
oral_defense_qna.answer: Domain C (Hierarchical Target Encodings) contributed ~60% of total gain, followed by Domain A (Store Geometry & Metadata) at ~18%, and Domain B (Calendar & Surge Flags) at ~14%. Macroeconomic and markdown indicators contributed under 8% combined.

oral_defense_qna.question: What is the inference latency and computational footprint of the champion model?
oral_defense_qna.answer: The trained XGBoost model artifact is 21.7 MB. Scoring all 115,064 records in the test set takes 0.47 seconds on standard CPU (4.08 microseconds per prediction, or ~245,000 predictions per second), making it lightweight enough to deploy on low-cost serverless microservices without GPUs.

oral_defense_qna.question: Can store managers use this model to claim that increasing markdowns caused higher sales?
oral_defense_qna.answer: No. This is strictly a predictive forecasting model, not a causal inference model. Markdowns correlate with higher sales because managers strategically schedule discounts during high-traffic holiday periods. Claiming causality without an A/B test or instrumental variable analysis would commit a post-hoc fallacy.

oral_defense_qna.question: What hyperparameter in XGBoost was most critical for preventing overfitting?
oral_defense_qna.answer: `min_child_weight = 12` combined with L1 leaf regularization (`reg_alpha = 0.4018`). By requiring at least 12 weighted observations per leaf, the tree was prohibited from splitting on noisy individual transactions or rare return weeks.

oral_defense_qna.question: What are the ethical implications of using automated sales forecasts in retail operations?
oral_defense_qna.answer: Retail shift scheduling and staffing hours are often directly tied to forecasted department demand. Volatile or under-predicted sales can lead to understaffing, overworking employees, or last-minute shift cancellations. We recommend automated forecasts be paired with human review and minimum shift stability guardrails.
